hook.pre_tool_use_commit_order.denied:
[Guardian:CommitOrder] The user's words this turn contain no version-control order keyword ({keywords}...); git commit was blocked.
If the user authorized in ordinary words (e.g. "OK, commit it"): when you judge it is an authorization, add a line `{auth_line}` to the command; the program checks that the quote appears verbatim in this turn's user words and that its clause is not negated ("don't commit yet" does not count).
Contract (USER.md shorthand commands): do not touch git before the order keyword. First list in the closing report "which files changed + what was verified / not verified", wait for the user to read the diff and say the order keyword, then commit and push in one go; never commit first and wait to push.
Memory directories (root / project / org layers) are not covered by the "memory-related goes straight in" manual commit: the vcs-sync worker commits and pushes automatically at harvest and session end, so the AI neither touches nor asks.
Only the user's own words count, after background notifications, other sessions' messages and system injections are stripped; if a message mixes in such blocks or tag text and is rejected as a whole, ask the user to type the keyword again on its own (only the latest user message counts; a system notification or background event in between means the keyword must be given again).
If the user really asked for it this turn: quote their words and ask them to repeat the keyword; for a lasting change adjust workflow/config.json guard.commit_order.keywords (enabled=false disables this gate).

hook.pre_tool_use_commit_order.hint_exem: If this commit is in the atom-memory system's own repo (or its worktree): the exemption only accepts a whole command chained with `&&`, whose first segment may be `cd <absolute path>` and every other segment is `git [-C <literal path>] add|commit|push|status|diff|log|show|rm|mv|restore ...`; remove pipes, `;` and command substitution and issue the commit command on its own, and no order keyword is needed. For a multi-line message feed a quoted heredoc to `git commit -F - <<'EOF'` (nothing after EOF on the opening line); the line after the closing EOF may carry another git chain such as push or log, but no further commit.
hook.pre_tool_use_commit_order.hint_wrap: No direct git commit could be parsed out this time; a commit may be hidden inside a wrapper (bash -c, powershell -Command, cmd /c...) or an expansion ($(), backticks, eval, parentheses). A command that contains an expansion such as `$()` and the word commit always needs the order keyword; if it is only a query, remove the word commit or use single quotes.

[Guardian:ScanReport] You declared the work done and this session touched core files or many files (past the closing-check threshold), but this turn did not emit anti_evasion_report, which breaks the anti-evasion contract in IDENTITY.
Call the MCP tool anti_evasion_report to submit the closing check. Its content goes to the HUD; chat keeps only a collapsed chip. The reader is a user who did not watch the process: write the body in plain language and put file:line / commit in each item's tech field or in (a)(g).
  Three groups, kept apart, all required: goal = what the user asked for this time, one item per request, each carrying the user's own words (said), what was done (done), how it was confirmed (verified, with numbers), and what was not done with the reason (not_done); principles = trade-offs that touch the user's long-term principles or direction (give [] if none); ai_decided = things the user did not ask for and you decided yourself: trade-offs, changes outside the requested scope, unverified assumptions, environment changes (give [] if none). The HUD compares the weight of the three groups, so a one-line mention of what the user asked for next to a long list of self-decided work is obvious at a glance.
  (a) Technical appendix, what was changed where: `- file:line — what changed`; write "none" if nothing. **Required**
  (b) AI evasion report: whether you ignored or buried anything this time; **fill only when it happened**, otherwise "none"
  (d) Memory intake ledger: first scan five sources — (1) things the user corrected, sent back, or repeated (2) mechanisms or pitfalls that took 2 or more retries or a lookup to understand (3) facts looked up outside (with the date) (4) trade-offs, contracts, or preferences I made (5) existing atoms proven wrong or needing a patch — then for each item write `- <item> → written to atom <name>` or `→ not written (one-line reason)`; anything worth writing must be written with atom_write **before** calling the tool, ⛔ "not written yet / see next action" will be blocked. **Required**, "none" if nothing
  (g) Technical appendix, version-control closing: what is committed, what is not and why (concurrent progress / awaiting a decision / privacy); "none" if nothing changed. **Required**
  (h) Closing verdict: one sentence — "can close" or "next action = ..." (list only what the user has to do; writing atoms, adding tests, committing are things you can do yourself, so do them first). **Required**
  (i) Derived scratch list: **one path per line** `<path> — <note>` (absolute or relative to cwd, globs allowed); list only what still exists now and awaits the user's decision, not what was deleted, and not pure explanations (default is delete when done); **Required**, "none" if nothing
  (j) Persistent evidence path: where this turn's verification receipts persist (usually `workflow/verify-ledger/<sid>.jsonl`, or the verification output file); if this session ran any sentinel verification you **must fill a path that really exists** (the Stop reconcile gate checks exists); write "none" only when there are no receipts
  (k) Follow-ups: things not finished that need chasing, one per line (saved into the closing report for the HUD); write "none" if there are none, **an empty string is not accepted**
The three groups plus a, b, d, g, h, i, j, k are all required; write "none" for what did not happen ((c), (e), (f) do not exist); if this turn already delivered a harvest report, (d) may say just "see harvest report". Do not wave it away with prose like "out of scope / left for the future".
